raw_response:
*Settling in to think as the farmer...*

---

Well, I've been working this same 8.5 mu for forty years now, since I took over from my father. It's just me and the old wife in the house — kids moved off to town, don't come back to help much except maybe at cotton picking. So whatever I plant, me and her have to be able to handle it ourselves.

I'll split the ground the same way I've been doing. About 5 mu of the better land — flatter, heavier soil — I do wheat then maize, same as everybody on our side of the village. The other 3.5 mu out west, that sandy patch, I keep in cotton. Cotton does alright on that ground and I've got buyers I know. I thought about dropping the cotton a few years back when prices were bad, but the neighbors are still growing it so I stuck with it. Old habit.

**Wheat (5 mu):** Plant around mid-October, after the maize comes off. I use seed I bought from the agro-shop — local variety, about 15 jin per mu, my son says I should try the new kind but I don't know it. Before planting I spread one bag of 二铵 (DAP, 50 jin) for every 2 mu or so, that's the base fertilizer, always done it that way. Then after the wheat wakes up in spring — around 返青 — I scatter urea, maybe half a bag per mu, and water it in. If the wheat looks yellow or thin at jointing I put down a bit more, but usually not. I irrigate before winter to help it through the cold, then返青水, then once more at filling if it's dry. Three times usually, four if the spring is dry. I spray once against those little bugs and the weeds — my neighbor 老王 tells me what to buy. Harvest early June with the combine, pay by the mu.

**Maize (5 mu, after wheat):** Tight turnaround — I've got maybe 5-6 days between wheat combine and getting maize in. No time to plow, I just direct-seed into the stubble with the little planter I hire from 老赵. Use a compound fertilizer, one bag per 2 mu as starter with the seed. Then at big trumpet stage (大喇叭口) I sidedress urea, about half a bag per mu. Maize usually doesn't need much water if the summer rains come, but if it's dry in July I'll irrigate once. Harvest end of September, shell it at home.

**Cotton (3.5 mu):** This is the one that takes real work. Plant late April after the soil warms up. I use the seed I bought last year from the same shop — they know me. Before planting I spread a bag of compound fertilizer and some manure I got from 老李's pigs. Cotton needs spraying a lot — bollworms, aphids — I'll spray maybe 6, 7 times across the season, whenever I walk the field and see trouble. Two irrigations: one at budding, one at flowering. The picking is the hardest — me and the wife work through October, sometimes into November. Three pickings. That's why I don't plant more than 3.5 mu, my back can't take it anymore.

Money is tight. Last year after everything, I cleared maybe 3,000 yuan from the wheat-maize and a little more from the cotton. This year I don't plan to change much. When you don't have extra money you don't experiment.
